stories.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: At least 11 Malaysians missing, Malaysian military ready to assist: Defence minister
stories.summary: Malaysia's embassy in Kathmandu is actively coordinating with local authorities.
article_sentences: At least 11 Malaysians are missing after severe floods hit Nepal’s Rasuwa district, causing over 160 deaths and widespread destruction.
Malaysia’s embassy in Kathmandu is coordinating with local authorities and rescue teams to locate the missing Malaysians and ensure their safety.
Malaysians in Nepal are advised to stay vigilant, avoid risky areas, update contact details via e-Konsular, and follow local safety instructions.
About a dozen Malaysians are among hundreds of people still missing after massive floods hit Nepal’s Rasuwa district, destroying villages and leaving at least 160 dead.

Malaysia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that it had received reports from the embassy in Kathmandu that contact had been lost with 11 Malaysians believed to be in the badly affected Rasuwa district, near the Nepal-China border.
Nepali authorities, however, said 17 Malaysians were among more than 300 foreigners reported missing from the affected areas.
Houses, cars and buildings have been swept away in a deluge of water after an avalanche further in the snowy-mountains triggered massive floods in the valley.

The swollen river also caused widespread damage to roads, bridges, electricity and communication infrastructure in affected areas, causing loss of contact with Malaysians there, said the foreign ministry.

“The embassy is actively coordinating with local authorities and the search and rescue teams currently being deployed by the Nepalese government to locate the affected Malaysians and ascertain their safety,” the ministry said in a statement.
National news agency Bernama reported that families have been unable to contact more than 50 Malaysian travellers in Nepal.
“We are still gathering information on the Malaysians who are unreachable.
Family members have been unable to establish contact with more than 50 Malaysians,” the charge d’affaires of the Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu, Mohd Firdaus Azman, told Bernama late on Aug 26.

stories.title: (LEAD) S. Korea to launch homegrown Nuri rocket on Oct. 7
stories.summary: South Korea's homegrown Nuri rocket will be launched on Oct. 7 for its mission to put 15 satellites into orbit, the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) said Thursday. The launch will take place at the Naro Space Center in the country's southern coastal village of Goheung, some 473 kilometers south of Seoul, between 12:23 p.m. and 1:23 p.m., with the exact time to be decided on the launch date, KASA said. The backup launch window has been set between Oct. 8 and Oct. 14. It will mark the fifth launch of the homegrown space rocket since the first launch carried out on Oct. 2021. At the time, the rocket failed to enter orbit while carrying a 1.5-ton dummy satellite. In June 2022, South Korea made the second attempt, which successfully put a Performance Verification Satellite (PVSAT) and a 1.3-ton dummy satellite into orbit. The third launch was held in May 2023, with South Korea successfully putting a next-generation small satellite and seven cube satellites into orbit. In its fourth launch, held in November 2025, the country successfully put 13 satellites into space. For the upcoming fifth launch, the Nuri rocket will hold 15 satellites, including a nano satellite constellation comprising five spacecraft. The satellites are currently undergoing a function check at the center, KASA added.
